text.content:
A mortal conduit for an ancient, often malevolent being that works its will through them in the waking world.

SKILLS

COMMISERATE · SL max 5

Whenever you hit only one creature with an attack or offensive [Z] spell and you share at least one status effect with that creature, if you lose Mind Points as part of the attack or offensive [Z] spell you lose (SL) less, to a minimum of 1 Mind Point.

BLOOD RITE · SL max 3

As a free action during your turn, you may lose up to (10 × SL) Hit Points to immediately fill a section of your Favour clock for every 10 Hit Points lost, which can exceed the maximum of your Favour clock. Any excess filled sections of your Favour beyond the maximum are erased at the end of the scene.

EPIPHANY · SL max 3

When you or an ally fails a Ritual of any discipline whose effects fall within your Patron's domains, you may erase up to (SL × 2) sections of your Favour clock to add a bonus to the Ritual's Magic Check equal to (the number of erased clock sections), potentially turning the triggering Check into a success.

HIGHER POWER · SL max 5

When you first gain this Skill, you gain a single Patron of your choice, gaining their Urge and their Blessing, as well as a 6-section Favour clock which starts with 2 filled sections.

Each time you gain this Skill, gain access to two Patron Boons of your choice following the rules detailed below. You may only have up to half (rounded up) of your total Boons active at any time, which you may choose when you rest or by erasing one section of your Favour clock to swap them during any scene as an action.

PROFANE RITUAL

You may spend a Fabula Point or erase 4 sections of your Favour clock to produce a token of your Patron as a powerful ingredient in a Ritual, as long as the Ritual results in an effect relating to the domains of your Patron. This ingredient is consumed, and can only be produced again once you have rested in a city or large settlement.

PATRONS

Once per session, your Patron may attempt to inflict its Urge at any time. The more you comply, the greater the reward; minor changes to your behaviour may award 0–1 sections but fully committing to the Urge may fill up to 2 sections, possibly even 4. You may also attempt to obey without prompting from your Urge at any time.

  • If you meaningfully or repeatedly obey, the GM may fill in 1–2 sections of your Favour clock.
  • If you meaningfully or repeatedly disobey, the GM may erase 1–2 sections of your Favour clock but you gain a Fabula Point.
  • If you skirt around the Urge or just barely comply, the GM may fill or erase 0–1 sections of your Favour clock.
  • If you obey in a pivotal way, the GM may fill up to 4 sections of your Favour clock.
  • If you disobey in a pivotal way, the GM may erase up to 4 sections of your Favour clock. If they do, they must grant you a Fabula Point.

If your Favour clock is ever empty, your Patron gains a consumable Opportunity to do one of the following:

  • Spend an Ultima Point to force you to adhere to your Urge, with no chance to willingly resist. Any willing party member may spend a Fabula Point to roll a contested (WLP + WLP) check against your Patron, with the number of successes determining how well they help you fight back. Past and present allies may do this even if they are not present in the scene, or have Sacrificed.
  • Spend an Ultima Point to remove access to your Boons for a scene, or until your Favour clock rises above 0, whichever comes first.
  • Spend an Ultima Point to cause your Boons to go haywire, choosing a Consequence from the Surrender table. This option can only be chosen in agreement with the Player.
  • Spend an Ultima Point to turn you into a magical beacon, alerting any magically sensitive enemies to your exact location.
  • Spend an Ultima Point to whisper your secrets to a villain in their dreams.

Once your Patron runs out of Ultima Points, or when the GM deems it thematically fitting, the GM may give you a quest to make the power become your own. Describe how you claim it for yourself, and design a more positive Patron and Urge (this can be a more benevolent entity, a being of your own creation, or simply your own soul). Note that even when the new Urge is created, it should still be something that is negative in large amounts; the Urge may still overpower you and lead you to make mistakes if your Favour clock is low. Things such as "You must never cling to personal belongings; give everything you can away" seem good in a moral "generosity" sense, but as an Urge may lead you to give away critical items or zenit your quest needs.

PATRON BOONS

Patron Boons are modular, passive effects that signify your Patron's reward for garnering their favour. At least half (rounded up) of your Boons must originate from your chosen Patron, the rest may be taken from other lists.

You may change the base damage types of the Patrons if it suits your character (such as changing Nergal to fire damage, or Apsu to earth damage).

Nergal, the Deathless Ground — Domains: earth, silence, space, eternity.

Urge: You must always stand your ground. Never submit, retreat, or back down, regardless of the consequences.

Blessing: You gain a bonus Hit Point pool equal to (2 × SL in Higher Power), carried on your innate Guise.

Boons:

  • Unyielding Resilience: When you activate this Boon, choose Defense or Magic Defense. You gain a +2 to the chosen defense, which does not stack with qualities or shields.
  • Unending Earth: Rituals you participate in to move earth and stone, erect structures, silence sound, or create barriers have their total Mind Point cost reduced by (5 × the filled sections on your Favour clock).
  • Unwavering Vigil: Creatures cannot be immune to melee attacks from you due to invisibility, camouflage, or stealth as long as they are not flying.

Baraqiel, the Crowned Storm — Domains: bolt, power, fear, rulership.

Urge: Maintain your pride. You must never bow to or admit inferiority to anyone, regardless of the consequences.

Blessing: You gain the ability to travel twice as fast when travelling, covering 2 travel days' worth of distance in a single travel day, and may move within a scene at blinding speeds.

Boons:

  • Thunderous Authority: You gain a bonus to any Checks that rely on your reputation and authority equal to the number of filled sections on your Favour clock. If you would fill or erase a section of a social interaction Clock with such a check, you fill or erase 1 additional section of that clock.
  • Blinding Presence: At the start of any conflict scene, or as an action outside of conflict, you may spend (5 × ½ the number of empty sections of your Favour clock) Mind Points to deal 10 damage of your Patron's damage type to all enemies nearby. You may choose to do no damage and simply summon a deafening and blinding flash of power, which costs half as many Mind Points and lasts for a few moments or one round in a conflict scene.
  • Absolute Power: You deal bonus damage with all offensive [Z] spells equal to the number of filled sections on your Favour clock, but also deal half of that bonus damage rounded up to yourself ignoring affinities. You must change the damage of any offensive [Z] spell you cast to your Patron's damage type.

Penemue, the Cold Archivist — Domains: ice, knowledge, mutation, dreams.

Urge: You must never forsake the pursuit of knowledge in the face of safety or ethics, even if it hurts the ones you love.

Blessing: All beings can understand your speech, even if they are not sentient, though you may not necessarily be able to understand them.

Boons:

  • Hell Frozen Over: Rituals you participate in to freeze or slow things, summon ice, clear the mind, or scry with water or ice have their total Mind Point cost reduced by (5 × the filled sections on your Favour clock).
  • Cold Calculation: You become Immune to the dazed status effect and you may treat your INS die as one size larger as long as half or more of your Favour clock is filled.
  • Chilling Revelation: You may erase 3 sections of your Favour clock at the end of your turn to have the GM tell you the exact details of the next action an enemy will take after your turn, as if you had used the Study action on it preemptively.

Azazel, the Vengeful Radiance — Domains: light, death, metal, vengeance.

Urge: You must feed your vengeance. You must never spare or forgive an enemy you have sworn condemnation against, regardless of redemption.

Blessing: Choose one creature type from the following: demon, elemental, undead. You may spend a minute to become aware of the rough estimate number and direction of any creature of that type within a travel day's distance around you.

Boons:

  • Perfect Judgement: Rituals you participate in to determine truth, detect hidden things, imprison creatures, or contain effects have their total Mind Point cost reduced by (5 × the filled sections on your Favour clock).
  • Perfect Blasphemy: When you activate this boon, choose one creature type from the following: demon, elemental, undead. You deal bonus damage with attacks and free attacks equal to (½ the filled sections on your Favour clock) against creatures of that type. You must change the damage type of any of your weapon Attacks to your Patron's damage type.
  • Perfect Doctrine: When you activate this boon, choose an ally. That ally gains the benefits of one of your active boons that is not Perfect Doctrine until you deactivate this boon.

Erra, the Devouring Fire — Domains: fire, chaos, war, destruction.

Urge: You must give into your rage and cause as much damage as possible, regardless of the collateral effects.

Blessing: You may willingly suffer the enraged status effect at any time. While enraged, treat your MIG die as being one size bigger.

Boons:

  • Eldritch Rampage: You gain a unique brawling weapon that replaces an unarmed strike. This weapon rolls (MIG + WLP) for its Accuracy Check formula, and deals (HR + 5 + ½ the filled sections of your Favour clock) damage of your Patron's element.
  • Rip And Tear: Rituals you participate in to burn or melt things, summon magma or fire, break or shatter things, or cause widespread devastation have their total Mind Point cost reduced by (5 × the filled sections on your Favour clock).
  • Lash Out: You start every scene enraged as long as this boon is activated. As long as you are enraged, you gain a bonus to the Accuracy Check of any heavy or brawling weapons you use equal to (½ the filled sections of your Favour clock).

Nasu, the Pestilent Marsh — Domains: poison, nature, rot, undeath.

Urge: You must never heal or redeem things that are rotting or dying due to age, illness, or poison.

Blessing: You become Immune to the poisoned condition, which cannot be ignored.

Boons:

  • Icon of Decay: Rituals you participate in to summon or kill plants, create poisons or acids, summon insects, or control plagues have their total Mind Point cost reduced by (5 × the filled sections on your Favour clock).
  • Vile Constitution: Your blood is incredibly volatile, dealing damage of your Patron's damage type equal to (the filled sections of your Favour clock) to any creature that hits you with a melee attack.
  • Metastasis: If an enemy is poisoned, and you were the one that applied the poisoned status effect to them, you may deal damage of your Patron's damage type equal to (the filled sections of your Favour clock) to the enemy once at the start of each of your turns.

Algea, the Well of Anguish — Domains: physical, pain, fear, amnesia.

Urge: You must never give a sworn enemy a swift death; you must humiliate and hurt them, mentally or physically.

Blessing: Physical damage you deal treats any affinity to physical damage higher than Resistance as Resistance. Effects you have that lower affinity or ignore Resistance apply to this new affinity, not the target's base affinity.

Boons:

  • Divine Suffering: When you activate this boon, erase three sections of your Favour clock. You gain resistance to physical damage this scene.
  • That Awful Flesh: While you are in Crisis, you automatically recover Hit Points at the end of your turn equal to (½ the filled sections of your Favour clock).
  • Skin Deep: As a free action you may lose (3 × the empty sections of your Favour clock) Hit Points to recover from a single status effect of your choice.

Apsu, the Drowned Secret — Domains: dark, water, deceit, secrets.

Urge: You must never leave a secret you know of alone, regardless of morality, safety, or consequences.

Blessing: Whenever you fill or erase sections of a social or stealth Clock, if your approach relied on trickery, stealth, deceit, or sabotage, fill or erase 2 additional sections of that Clock.

Boons:

  • Masks Upon Masks: Rituals you participate in to create illusions, modify memories, hide or alter information, or control darkness have their total Mind Point cost reduced by (5 × the filled sections on your Favour clock).
  • Depths of Deception: A creature whose WLP is less than yours can never tell if you are lying without the aid of lie-detection magic, and you may treat your WLP die as 1 size larger as long as half or more of your Favour clock is filled.
  • Liar's Blade: As part of any Attack, you may spend (5 × the number of empty sections of your Favour clock) Mind Points to target all targets' Magic Defense instead of their Defense.

Az, the Hoarding Engine — Domains: air, machines, greed, wealth.

Urge: You must never give in to charitable or generous impulses, and must hoard your wealth and power for yourself.

Blessing: You may recover (½ the filled sections of your Favour clock) Inventory Points for free when you rest in a city or settlement.

Boons:

  • Cog In The Machine: Rituals you participate in to set triggers and traps, manipulate machinery, summon wind, or alter weather have their total Mind Point cost reduced by (5 × the filled sections on your Favour clock).
  • Clockwork Heart: You count as a construct creature, and other construct creatures can never start out hostile to you unless already aware that you are an enemy. Other allies do not gain this benefit (unless via Perfect Doctrine or other similar effects).
  • Sinful Hoard: Whenever you gain or earn at least 50 zenit, you gain or earn an additional (5 × the filled sections of your Favour clock) zenit. Whenever you gain at least 50 zenit worth of raw materials, increase their value by an additional (5 × the filled sections of your Favour clock) zenit.

Apep, the Unmaking — Domains: nothingness, void, entropy. Whenever you use this Patron's damage type, roll a d8 to randomly determine the damage type.

Urge: Stop caring, and suppress your desire to bond and connect with others. Remain alone, even when surrounded by others.

Blessing: Once per round you may erase a section of your Favour clock to change any one instance of damage taken by any creature into your Patron's damage type before affinities. If it ends up as the same damage type, it becomes typeless.

Boons:

  • Void: Rituals you participate in to erase matter, teleport, manipulate gravity, or warp space have their total Mind Point cost reduced by (5 × the filled sections on your Favour clock).
  • Null: While you are present in a scene, any damage taken by any creature that does not have a type is halved, and has a maximum of the victim's Crisis score.
  • Chaos: At the start of every scene while this boon is active, randomly rearrange your Affinities (but do not change the type; for example, if you have 2 Vulnerabilities and 1 Immunity, simply reassign those affinities rather than changing their intensity).

Generic Boons (you may choose from this list, counting it as if it belonged to your Patron)

  • Eldritch Versatility: You may change the damage type of any spell you cast to your Patron's damage type by increasing the total Mind Point Cost by 5.
  • Eldritch Transmutation: You may transmute any part of your body, up to your entire body, into your Patron's element at will. You gain the ability to make unarmed strikes even if you have no free and/or empty hands. Your unarmed strikes become ranged and their damage type changes to your Patron's damage type.
  • Eldritch Kinesis: You may crudely summon and/or telekinetically control simple masses of your Patron's element within a very short distance of yourself as an action, without the need of a Ritual. You gain access to the offensive [Z] spell Kinetic Projectile, and cannot deal damage with these masses unless you use Kinetic Projectile.
  • Eldritch Sorcery: You gain access to the unique spell Eldritch Burst.
  • Eldritch Armaments: You may summon a copy of any basic weapon or shield (simple or martial) without a Quality at will. When you do, choose physical damage or your Patron's damage type; the weapon's damage type changes to the type chosen. If the damage type chosen is not physical and the weapon is not an arcane weapon, you must spend (2 × the empty sections of your Favour clock) Mind Points as part of summoning the weapon. The weapon vanishes when you unequip it until you re-equip it, and cannot be wielded by any creature other than you. This weapon lasts until you summon a different weapon or you deactivate this boon.
  • Eldritch Affinity: When you activate this boon, choose one of your Patron's damage types. As long as the type is not physical, you gain Resistance to that type while this boon is active.
  • Eldritch Immunity: When you activate this boon, choose one of your Patron's damage types. As long as the type is not physical, you gain Immunity to that type but a Vulnerability to its complementary type while this boon is active.
  • Eldritch Absorption: When you activate this boon, choose one of your Patron's damage types. As long as the type is not physical, you now Absorb that type but gain Vulnerability to two of its complementary types while this boon is active.
  • Eldritch Expansion: Choose one damage type from another Patron. Your Patron now counts that damage type among its own damage types.
  • Eldritch Influence: Choose one additional Urge from another Patron. Your Patron can reward you for obeying this Urge.
  • Agonizing Burst: Eldritch Burst's Cost changes to "30 MP or Erase six sections of your Favour clock" and its damage becomes "20 damage of your Patron's damage type."

Spells

Eldritch Burst — Cost: 15 MP or erase three sections of your Favour clock (after the spell is resolved). Target: up to three creatures. Duration: Instantaneous.

This spell always hits, and cannot be forced to miss by any effect. Each target suffers 10 damage of your Patron's damage type. This spell counts as an offensive spell for the purposes of Skills and Qualities.

Kinetic Projectile [Z] — Cost: (10 × T) or erase one section of your Favour clock per target (after the spell is resolved). Target: up to three creatures. Duration: Instantaneous.

This targets Defense instead of Magic Defense. Each target suffers (HR + 10) damage of the damage type used in Eldritch Kinesis. This spell deals an additional 5 damage for every 3 filled sections of your Favour clock. Then, the target suffers one of the following status effects based on the damage type: Physical, earth: slow. Fire, ice: weak. Bolt, light: dazed. Dark, poison: shaken.

RULES

  • You gain the ability to perform Occultism Rituals related to your Patron’s domains. Occultism Rituals use \[WLP \+ WLP\] for their magic check.
